newsitem.title: USA: Fla jury recommends death for alleged serial killer.
newsitem.headline: Fla jury recommends death for alleged serial killer.

text.p: A Florida jury Friday recommended the death penalty for alleged serial killer Glen Rogers, convicted in the slaying of a hotel maid and suspected in the deaths of three other women during a 1995 cross-country killing spree.

The 12-member jury deliberated for about three hours before returning a unanimous decision that Rogers should die in Florida's electric chair for the slaying of Tina Marie Cribbs, a mother of two who met Rogers at a bar and offered him a ride to a nearby carnival.
"We're going to try to pick up the pieces of whatever is left of our lives and go on," said Cribbs' mother, Mary Dicke, after the recommendation was announced.
Hillsborough County Judge Diane Allen, who has the final decision, set sentencing for June 20.

Rogers, a 34-year-old Ohio native, was captured in Kentucky in November 1995, two days after Cribbs' body was discovered in a Tampa motel room. He was driving Cribbs' Ford Fiesta and was caught after a high-speed chase.
Authorities say Rogers also killed Sandra Gallagher in Van Nuys, California, Linda Price in Jackson, Mississippi, and Andy Sutton in Bossier City, Louisiana, between September and November 1995.
Kentucky authorities also want to talk to him about the 1993 death of his former roommate, Mark Peters, 71.
The jury deliberated for about seven hours Wednesday before finding Rogers guilty of Cribbs' murder.
During a two-day sentencing hearing, prosecutor Karen Cox asked jurors to recommend the death penalty, calling it a "fine example of a case where the punishment should fit the crime."
Rogers' attorneys told jurors their client had been abused as a child, suffered from a mental illness and had had a series of head injuries.
"The state wants to cook him. The state wants to destroy his mind and body, one of God's creatures," defence attorney Robert Frazier said.
